newsitem.title: ROMANIA: U.S. lawmakers feed Romania's NATO hopes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers feed Romania's NATO hopes.

text.p: Romania's hopes of joining NATO have been boosted by a supporting letter from two U.S. lawmakers to President Bill Clinton, a Foreign Ministry official said on Friday.

"The letter publicly acknowledges the democratic changes in our country," Sorin Ducaru, head of the Romanian Foreign Ministry's NATO and WEU department, told journalists. "It also shows that Romania meets all NATO admission criteria."
Senator Alfonse D'Amato and Representative Christopher Smith wrote to Clinton this week asking that Romania be included in the first wave of NATO expansion at the Madrid summit in July.
Romania's centrist coalition government, which ended seven years of leftist rule in last year's elections, has made NATO membership its main political goal.
But former Warsaw Pact members Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are seen as favorites in NATO expansion. Slovenia is also a possible candidate.

France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Greece and Turkey have expressed public support for Romania's bid to win early admission. But the United States, Britain and Germany have so far given no such explicit support.
"The letter confirms our chances are growing," Ducaru said.
